What you're looking at

Earlier versions of this map traced each province from the mod's hand-drawn provinces.bmp and warped its exact shape onto real latitude/longitude with a fitted thin-plate spline. That gets every province's shape close to the mod's intent, but its borders are only ever an approximation of the vanilla map — TPS residual error, however small, means a tinted province and the vanilla outline underneath it never quite agree.

This version trades shape fidelity for exact alignment instead. Every province's centroid (from that same warped fit) becomes a seed on a fine lon/lat grid rasterized directly from eu4.json's own vanilla polygons — so the grid is the old map, not an approximation of it. Assignment happens in two contained passes rather than one global race: each vanilla polygon is first split only among the mod provinces that actually seeded inside it (a mod province can no longer bleed into a neighboring vanilla polygon just for being the nearest seed overall — it only ever competes within the one polygon it mapped to), via a weighted flood fill (a marker-based watershed) that charges extra to cross water, so a peninsula across a narrow strait isn't handed to a seed on the opposite shore just because it's closer as the crow flies. Any vanilla polygon that got no seed at all is then filled in from its nearest already-assigned neighbor. Because no cell outside eu4.json's own landmass is ever assigned to anything, the union of every province here is pixel-for-pixel identical to the vanilla coastline — new internal borders, but zero drift at the edges.

Regenerate with scripts/build-mod-province-geojson.py (the warped fit) then scripts/build-mod-province-aligned.py (this grid snap) · output geo-explorer/public/eu4-extended-timeline-aligned.json.
